entities.name: FliF flagellar M ring
observations: The 560-residue query sequence is an exact sequence match to reviewed Salmonella typhimurium FliF (UniProt P15928).
FliF is the flagellar basal-body MS/M-ring protein and may participate in energy transduction.
It is an integral inner-membrane, multi-pass-associated flagellar basal-body component.
The sequence contains Pfam FliF_N at residues 51–105, YscJ_FliF at 114–221, and YscJ_FliF_C at 253–437.
Curated annotations associate FliF with bacterial flagellum basal body, plasma membrane, cytoskeletal motor activity, and flagellum-dependent cell motility.

entities.name: FliF E. coli
observations: Escherichia coli FliF (UniProt P25798) is a close reviewed homolog with 86.3% identity and 99.1% query coverage.
The homolog is annotated as an inner-membrane flagellar M-ring protein involved in basal-body assembly and possible energy transduction.

entities.name: Bacterial flagellum-dependent motility
observations: FliF is a structural component of the bacterial flagellar basal body and contributes to flagellum-dependent cell motility.
The basal body includes L, P, S, and M rings mounted on a central rod; FliF forms the M/MS ring in the inner membrane.

entities.name: Bacterial inner membrane
observations: FliF is localized to the bacterial plasma/inner membrane as part of the flagellar basal body.
